entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Al-Ghazali?
entries.text: Abū Ḥāmid Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-Ghazālī (1058-1111) (Persian: ابو حامد محمد ابن محمد الغزالی), often Algazel in English, was born and died in Tus, in the Khorasan province of Persia.
entries.title: Al-Ghazali

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Vladimir Lenin?
entries.text: Vladimir Ilyich Ulyanov (22 April 1870 – 21 January 1924), better known as Vladimir Lenin, was a Russian revolutionary, politician, and political theorist. He was the first leader of the Soviet Union, starting when the country was created in 1922.
entries.title: Vladimir Lenin

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Avicenna?
entries.text: Ibn Sina (Persian/Tajik: ابن سینا; 980 – June 1037 CE), commonly known in the West as Avicenna, was a Persian polymath and the most important doctor and Islamic philosopher of his time.
entries.title: Avicenna

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was James Prescott Joule?
entries.text: James Prescott Joule (24 December 1818 – 11 October 1889) was an English physicist, born in Salford, near Manchester. In his time he had great contribution to the world of electricity and thermodynamics.
entries.title: James Prescott Joule

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Gottfried Leibniz?
entries.text: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (also Leibnitz or von Leibniz) 1 July 1 (21 June OS) 1646 – 14 November 1716) was a German intellectual who wrote mostly in French and Latin.
entries.title: Gottfried Leibniz

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Leonardo da Vinci?
entries.text: Leonardo Da Vinci (15 April 1452 – 2 May 1519) was an Italian polymath who lived during the Renaissance. He is famous for his paintings.
entries.title: Leonardo da Vinci

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Pablo Picasso?
entries.text: Pablo Picasso (full name: Pablo Diego José Francisco de Paula Juan Nepomuceno María de los Remedios Cipriano de la Santísima Trinidad Ruiz y Picasso, October 25, 1881 – April 8, 1973) was a Spanish painter and sculptor. He created over 20,000 works of art.
entries.title: Pablo Picasso

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Truth?
entries.text: The truth is what is true. It may be everything that is true (reality) or just a part of it (a fact).
entries.title: Truth

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Man?
entries.text: A man is an adult male human. Culturally, he is considered the opposite of a woman.
entries.title: Man

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Diplomacy?
entries.text: Diplomacy is about relations between countries. For example, countries can make an agreement together, such as a treaty.
entries.title: Diplomacy

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Government?
entries.text: A government is a group of people that have the power to rule in a territory, according to the administrative law. This territory may be a country, a state or province within a country, or a region.
entries.title: Government

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Peace?
entries.text: Peace is a time without any fights or wars. In a larger sense, peace (or peacefulness) can mean a state of harmony, quiet or calm that is not disturbed by anything at all, like a still pond with no ripples.
entries.title: Peace

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Civil war?
entries.text: A civil war is a type of war that takes place between two or more groups in one country. While civil wars can take place for many reasons, there are two common reasons.
entries.title: Civil war

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Arabic language?
entries.text: Arabic (اَلْعَرَبِيَّةُ, al-ʿarabiyyah) is a Central Semitic language that first appeared in the mid-ninth century BCE in Northern Arabia and Sahara southern Levant. It is related to other Semitic languages like Hebrew and Aramaic.
entries.title: Arabic language

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Portuguese language?
entries.text: Portuguese (Portuguese: português) is a Romance language. It originated from Galician-Portuguese, which was first spoken in Northwestern Iberia.
entries.title: Portuguese language

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Sanskrit?
entries.text: Sanskrit (संस्कृत) is an ancient Indo-European language. Many languages in the Indian subcontinent today are derived from Sanskrit.
entries.title: Sanskrit

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Turkish language?
entries.text: Turkish (Türkçe) is a language that is officially spoken in Turkey and Cyprus. Turkish is the 18th most-spoken language in the world.
entries.title: Turkish language

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Fiction?
entries.text: Fiction is any story created by humans, originating from the depths of human imagination. It is not based on real-life events or actual people, but rather represents a departure from reality, allowing for the exploration of ideas, emotions, and scenarios that may not exist in the real world.
entries.title: Fiction

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease?
entries.text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), also known as chronic obstructive lung disease (COLD), and chronic obstructive airway disease (COAD), is a collection of obstructive pulmonary diseases which make breathing gradually more difficult.
entries.title: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Base?
entries.text: A base is a substance that can accept a hydrogen ion (H+) from another substance. A chemical can accept a proton if it has a negative charge, or if the molecule has an electronegative atom like oxygen, nitrogen, or chlorine that is rich in electrons.
entries.title: Base (chemistry)

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Weak interaction?
entries.text: Weak interaction, the weak force or weak nuclear force, is one of the four fundamental forces in the universe.
entries.title: Weak interaction

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Trigonometry?
entries.text: Trigonometry (from the Greek trigonon = three angles and metron = measure) is a part of elementary mathematics dealing with angles, triangles and trigonometric functions such as sine (abbreviated sin), cosine (abbreviated cos) and tangent (abbreviated tan).
entries.title: Trigonometry

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Computer?
entries.text: A computer is a machine that uses electronics to input, process, store, and output data. Data is information such as numbers, words, and lists.
entries.title: Computer

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Chess?
entries.text: Chess is a board game for two players. It is played on a square board, made up of 64 smaller squares, with eight squares in each row and column.
entries.title: Chess

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Ancient Greece?
entries.text: Ancient Greek civilization, also commonly called Ancient Greece, was a large area, mostly along the northeast shore of the Mediterranean Sea, where people spoke the Greek language. The area was much larger than today's country of Greece.
entries.title: Ancient Greece

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Gupta Empire?
entries.text: The Gupta Empire was an Indian empire which lasted from around 320 to 550 AD. It managed to unify large parts of the Indian subcontinent.
entries.title: Gupta Empire

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Roman Empire?
entries.text: The Roman Empire ruled the Mediterranean and much of Europe, Western Asia and North Africa. The Romans conquered most of this during the Republic, and it was ruled by emperors following Octavian's assumption of effective sole rule in 27 BC.
entries.title: Roman Empire

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Abbasid Caliphate?
entries.text: The Abbasid Caliphate was the third Arab Islamic caliphate. It overthrew the Umayyad caliphs from all but Al-Andalus.
entries.title: Abbasid Caliphate

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Mongol Empire?
entries.text: The Mongol Empire existed in the 13th and the 14th centuries and was one of the largest land empires in history.
entries.title: Mongol Empire

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Pakistan?
entries.text: Pakistan, officially the Islamic Republic of Pakistan (Urdu: Islāmī Jumhūriyah Pākistān), is a country in South Asia. It shares its border with other countries India, Iran, Afghanistan and China (disputed with India).
entries.title: Pakistan

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Brazil?
entries.text: Brazil, officially the Federative Republic of Brazil, is a country in South America. It is the world's fifth-largest country by area, behind Russia, Canada, the United States, and China, with a total area of 8,514,877 square kilometers (3,287,612 sq mi).
entries.title: Brazil

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.text: Jakarta, officially the Special Capital Region of Jakarta (Indonesian: Daerah Khusus Ibukota Jakarta shortened DKI Jakarta), is the largest and the capital city of Indonesia. entries.title: Jakarta

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.text: The Bab-el-Mandeb, meaning "Gate of Tears" in Arabic, is a strait between Yemen on the Arabian Peninsula, Djibouti and Eritrea, north of Somalia, in the Horn of Africa, and connecting the Red Sea to the Guardafui Channel and Gulf of Aden. entries.text: Burkina Faso (UK: Help:IPA/English /bɜːˌkiː.nə ˈfæs.əʊ/, US: /bʊrˌkiː.nə ˈfɑː.soʊ/) is a country in West Africa. It used to be called Upper Volta and the name was changed to Burkina Faso in 1984.

entries.text: Cosmology is the branch of astronomy that deals with the universe.

entries.text: A stellar black hole (or stellar-mass black hole) is a type of black hole formed by the gravitational collapse of a star.

entries.question: What is Convection?
entries.text: Convection is the movement of heat because of the movement of warm matter. Convection is defined as the method of heat transfer through a fluid from places of higher temperature to lower temperature by the movement of the molecules due to their different densities.

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Turbulence?
entries.text: Turbulence or turbulent flow is violent, unsteady, chaotic movement of fluids like air and water, and is contrasted with laminar flow.

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Ultrasound?
entries.text: Ultrasound (also called ultrasonography, computer echotomography, echography (or echotomography), and ultrasonic imaging) is a type of using sound to make images of what is under the skin (such as in pregnancy) or the blood vessels. entries.title: Rayleigh scattering

entries.text: The Roman Empire ruled the Mediterranean and much of Europe, Western Asia and North Africa. The Romans conquered most of this during the Republic, and it was ruled by emperors following Octavian's assumption of effective sole rule in 27 BC. The western empire collapsed in 476 AD, but the eastern empire, the Byzantine Empire, lasted until the fall of Constantinople in 1453. The Empire started in 27 BC, when Octavian became Emperor Augustus after the death of Julius Caesar. The fall of Western Roman Empire to the Germanic kings in 476 AD, marked the end of classical antiquity and the beginning of the Middle Ages. The Empire was the third stage of Ancient Rome. Rome was first ruled by Roman kings, later by the Roman Republic and then by an emperor. Many modern lands were once part of the Roman Empire such as, Britain (not Scotland), Spain, Portugal, France, Italy, Greece, Turkey, Germany, Egypt, Levant, Crimea, Switzerland and the northern coast of Africa. The main language of the Roman Empire was Latin, with Greek as an important secondary language, especially in the Eastern provinces. The Western half of the Roman Empire lasted for about 500 years until the barbarian general Odoacer defeated its final emperor, Romulus Augustus. On the other hand, the eastern half, consisting of the Balkans, Anatolia, The Levant and Egypt, continued for about 1000 more years before falling to the Ottomans. entries.text: Ancient Greek civilization, also commonly called Ancient Greece, was a large area, mostly along the northeast shore of the Mediterranean Sea, where people spoke the Greek language. The area was much larger than today's country of Greece. Greek civilization thrived, especially during the archaic period, between the 8th and the 6th centuries BC. It continued until 146 BC and ended with the Roman conquest of Greece at the Battle of Corinth.

entries.text: The Mongol Empire existed in the 13th and the 14th centuries and was one of the largest land empires in history. The original homeland of the Mongols was bounded by the Khingan Mountains to the east, the Altai and the Tian Mountains to the west, the Shilka River and the mountain ranges by Lake Baikal to the north, and the Great Wall of China to the south. It was founded by Genghis Khan in 1206 AD, when he brought together the Mongol and Turkic tribes. When he died in 1227 AD, he had conquered Central Asia, northern China, and parts of eastern Persia. Later, his grandson Kublai Khan went on to expand the empire and found the Mongol-ruled Yuan dynasty, which ruled and known over all of Chinese and it’s civilisation. The Mongol Empire stretched from Eastern Europe to East Asia, including Central Asia and some South East Asias.::.
